_comment: The river crossings (W20, floored and re-aimed W21). W20 centred them on the line but turned them with a mirrored formula (atan2(dx, -dz) for atan2(dx, dz)), so each stood 22-58 degrees off square and two had an end in the river's next leg; and they were floored at terrain max under a footprint lying wholly inside the cut, which is the riverbed, so every deck was under the water. Now: yaw is the true perpendicular to the reach each stands on; ground:"water" (Settlements) floors a site at the river's surface plus a clearance, or at the bank where that is higher; the layouts are 90 m, what the cut is across, and grow their own stairs down to whichever bank height they find. crossing_castle_road moved 85 m down its reach: at the 42-degree bend where it stood, a 90 m span has the other leg of the river under its far half whatever way it is turned, and the only spot left on the short leg put an end 27 m up the ridge skirt. The river runs along the ridge, so one end of crossing_west sits on the skirt's first metres; that end's bank is high and the far end gets the stair. The hanging bridge is at the Wide Water, where the owner asked for a span with no supports under it.
